title: Upper Bound
statement:
Given a sorted array of N integers (may contain duplicates) and a target T, find the **upper bound** — the index of the first element that is **strictly greater than** T.

If all elements are <= T, return N.

Implement using binary search in O(log N).

Use case: upper_bound - lower_bound gives the count of T in the array.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^7
-10^9 <= A[i] <= 10^9
Array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
-10^9 <= T <= 10^9
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and T.
Line 2: N space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: A single integer: the 0-indexed upper bound position.

examples.explanation: First index where A[i] > 5 is index 6 (value 7).
